summary: A performance and correctness release: thread-safe code stops paying a safety tax, constant tables stop bloating outputs, and module resolution gets several fixes.

highlights.title: Trusted atomics skip the safety trampoline
highlights.text: Hot loops built on the standard library's atomic primitives no longer pay the unsafe-confinement trampoline on every operation. Trusted primitives compile directly, so the thread-safe queue benchmark drops from seconds to milliseconds while the confinement guarantees still guard everything else.

highlights.title: Constant tables compile once, not per use
highlights.text: A module-level constant array is emitted once as a read-only global instead of being rebuilt on the stack at every reference. Large lookup tables (tens of thousands of entries) shrink both code size and compile time dramatically.

highlights.title: Byte buffers grow past 16 MB
highlights.text: The vector growth guard capped buffers at about 16 million elements, so a byte vector could not hold a 20 MB file. The ceiling is now 4 billion elements (32 GB for byte buffers); allocation failure remains the real limit.

highlights.title: Strings built inside methods are correct
highlights.text: A vector-of-strings field read inside a method could compile to integer arithmetic on pointers, producing garbage strings or a crash. Concatenation and accumulation in method bodies now call the string runtime like everywhere else.

highlights.title: Sibling imports work under the run command
highlights.text: Running a script now resolves modules next to the script exactly like checking it does; previously the temporary working copy hid the script's directory from the module catalog.

highlights.title: Standard-library atomics run at native speed
highlights.text: Atomic integer, boolean, and pointer operations in the standard library's sync module now compile directly, removing the per-call safety trampoline from tight thread-safe loops built on them.
